'''Bryce Byrum Reeve III''' (born December 31, 1968) is an American [[psychometrician]], [[Outcomes research|outcomes research scientist]], professor of Health Policy and Management at the [[UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health]] (with an adjunct appointment in the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience), and faculty expert at the [[UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center]]. He is a prominent figure in quantitative research on improving the measurement of [[Patient-reported outcome|patient-reported health outcomes]].

==Career==
A [[North Carolina]] native and graduate of [[Chapel Hill High School (Chapel Hill, North Carolina)|Chapel Hill High School]], Reeve earned a bachelor's degree with distinction from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]] in 1994 and subsequently worked for several years as a statistical consultant in the [[Research Triangle]] area. He returned to UNC to complete a master's (1999) and PhD (2000) in the L. L. Thurstone Psychometric Laboratory under [[David Thissen]].<ref>[http://sph.unc.edu/files/2013/07/reeve_hpmcv.pdf Bryce Reeve's curriculum vitae]</ref> Reeve's doctoral dissertation used [[item response theory]] to analyze data from the [[Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory]].

Upon earning his PhD, Reeve worked as a [[psychometrician]] and Program Director at the [[National Cancer Institute]]. He joined the [[UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health]] faculty in 2010, earning tenure four years later. He is currently Full Professor in the Department of Health Policy and Management; Research Fellow at the Cecil G. Sheps Center for Health Services Research; and Adjunct Associate Professor of [[Quantitative Psychology]] in the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience.

His record of extramural service includes advisory roles and board memberships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and private companies (e.g., [[PatientsLikeMe]]) dedicated to [[Patient participation|patient-centered care]] and [[Quality of life (healthcare)|health-related quality of life]].<ref>[https://www.openresearchexchange.com/advisors Scientific advisors, Open Research Exchange by PatientsLikeMe]</ref>

==Research==
Reeve has been a [[principal investigator]] on numerous grants from the [[National Institutes of Health]], the [[Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute]], and others.<ref>[https://sph.unc.edu/sph-news/nih-funds-unc-for-pediatric-patient-reported-outcomes-consortium/ ''NIH funds UNC for pediatric patient-reported outcomes consortium'']</ref> He leads the [[Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System]] research site at the University of North Carolina.<ref>[http://www.nihpromis.com/about/UniversityNorthCarolina PROMIS at the University of North Carolina]{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He has published hundreds of peer-reviewed journal articles on [[public health]] and [[patient-reported outcome]]s in addition to nearly one dozen books or book chapters and nearly a hundred abstracts and presentations at scholarly conferences. His work is known for [[statistics|statistical]] and [[psychometrics|psychometric]] rigor, particularly with respect to the application of [[item response theory]] to [[questionnaire]] design and analysis.

He has received six Awards of Merit from the [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] and, in 2015, received the John Ware and Alvin Tarlov Career Achievement Prize, a major international award for research in patient-reported outcomes.<ref>[https://unclineberger.org/newsletters/lineup/honors-and-awards/2015/reeve-awarded-the-john-ware-and-alvin-tarlov-career-achievement-prize-in-patient-reported-outcomes-measures ''Reeve awarded John Ware and Alvin Tarlov Career Achievement Prize in Patient-Reported Outcomes Measures'']</ref>
